subject: physical-education
title: Unit assessment: attempting the goal and evaluating the attempt under transfer
focus: attempting the goal and evaluating the attempt
essentialQuestion: What would I like to be genuinely good at, and what will that cost me?
materials: equipment appropriate to the chosen challenge
privacySafeScenario: Set, prepare for, and attempt one significant personal movement challenge chosen by the learner, then evaluate both the attempt and the preparation that led to it.
studentTask: Learner works attempting the goal and evaluating the attempt carried through an actual attempt at the goal, including a setback, and evaluated honestly afterwards at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of attempting the goal and evaluating the attempt degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds attempting the goal and evaluating the attempt carried through an actual attempt at the goal, including a setback, and evaluated honestly afterwards, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: The challenge is defined entirely by the learner relative to their own current capability; any goal that is meaningful and safe for that learner qualifies.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of attempting the goal and evaluating the attempt yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
The challenge is defined entirely by the learner relative to their own current capability; any goal that is meaningful and safe for that learner qualifies.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where attempting the goal and evaluating the attempt shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
